problems.memo_sentence: "The metric-based extension adds 10 extra connections versus 28 for an all-to-all extension, yet achieves better performance than randomly extended circuits with the same parameter count and even outperforms the all-to-all extension on the test set, where the latter shows clear overfitting; the authors interpret this as hinting at better generalization of the metric-based design."
problems.source_evidence: "The metric-based extension on the other hand shows the best performance on the test set, closely followed by the nearest-neighbor extension and random connections. While these observations hint at better generalization capabilities of the metric-based extension, an increasing slope can be observed. Therefore, the question whether these results hold with increasing training iterations or increasing circuit depth, remains open."
problems.explanation: The memo reports the test-set advantage but omits the nearby caveat that the metric-based curve still has an increasing slope and that generalization remains unconfirmed with more iterations or depth.

problems.memo_sentence: "For the JGB interest-rate data, restricting to 12 qubits and using variation of information, the metric-based heuristic produces a circuit with 13 additional gates that tend to connect bits within the same feature and yields lower training MMD than the linear baseline and random extensions, although the separation on the test set is less clear."
problems.source_evidence: "While being close to each other, the metric-based extension shows a better performance than random, which confirms the similar results of the BAS dataset. However, the separation between both loss curves is not as clear on the test set, which is why we did not include the graph."
problems.explanation: The memo captures the weaker test-set separation, but it omits the explicit methodological caveat that the test graph was not included because the separation was not clear.

problems.memo_sentence: "The authors state that problem-agnostic all-to-all circuit extensions, while showing promising gradient behavior, become infeasible to train on hardware with limited resources as problem size grows, motivating more parsimonious designs."
problems.source_evidence: "Although the problem-agnostic all-to-all circuit extension showed promising gradient behavior, as the problem size grows, it becomes infeasible to train on hardware with limited resources due to the constraints in the number of gates and compute time."
problems.explanation: The memo mentions hardware/resource infeasibility, but it drops the explicit reason that compute time also becomes a limiting factor. This is a concrete limitation stated in the paper.

problems.memo_sentence: "They further emphasize that they did not establish a mathematical connection between classical feature similarity, the entanglement capacity of the resulting circuits, and inductive bias, and that they did not investigate the impact of circuit depth, in particular repeating the extension layers, leaving open how depth interacts with their heuristic."
problems.source_evidence: "While this is the more fundamental open question for future research, we also suggest a path on the experimental side. As we only compared several circuits by connectivity, we did not focus on the effect of circuit depth, more specifically repeating the extension layer for each method."
problems.explanation: The memo captures the depth limitation, but it misses the paper's framing that this is a more fundamental open question for future research and that the authors only compared connectivity variants. That omission weakens the stated limitation.
